answer: An admission auction blocks a tide of fake identities by pricing entry. Each candidate anchors a bid deposit equal to twice its expected 20-epoch earnings, and only top bids win slots, so one operator cannot cheaply flood the market. A pulse reopens the auction every 10 epochs, forcing clones to rebid. Creating 100 fakes costs 100 deposits plus 100 bid fees, while an honest agent pays one deposit, recovers it on exit, and keeps rewards undiluted.
